test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In triangle ABC, AB = 15 { cm} , AC = 13 { cm} , and angle A = 90^circ . Find its area.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled triangle, the two sides containing the 90° angle act as the base and height.

Area = 1/2 × Product of legs

Area = 1/2 × 15 × 13

Area = 195 ÷ 2 = 97.5 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 97.5 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: AB = 15 cm, AC = 13 cm, and ∠A = 90°.

Formula: Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/778ee96cedc1a033ad2dfdf1abf40e5d88abb16cb852caa13af67e032b67b3f8.png] 

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠A = 90°

⇒ Base (AB) = 15 cm

⇒ Height (AC) = 13 cm

⇒ Area = 1/2 × AB × AC

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 15 × 13

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 195

⇒ Area = 97.5 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 97.5 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: BC² = AB² + AC².

Heron's Formula

For a triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c)/2.

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The radius of the circumcircle of a right-angled triangle is exactly half of its hypotenuse: R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2.
